output.brief: Resignations are concentrated on the large Kestrel matter: 8 of the 11 associates assigned to it have left, against 1 of the 13 who were not. The pay explanation does not hold up. Associates are paid at the 54th–61st percentile, the same as the rest of the firm. The rival firm's band is £3–5k higher, not £15k, and most leavers took equal or lower pay. The firm-wide target rise and normal market movement do not explain why only this group is affected. What remains unresolved is whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the supervision by Dorian Faulk. Every Kestrel associate reports to him and he supervises no one else, so the records cannot separate the two. The survey shows both problems: unsustainable workload and disrespectful treatment. I am fairly confident the cause lies in Kestrel, not pay. I am not confident which of the two it is. Do not announce the £12k payment or close the review. Commission the independent confidential interviews (about £9k, three weeks), designed to separate workload from supervision. In the meantime, add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Hold the supervision change and the contract reviewers until the interviews are back, unless more people resign before then.
